previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of recurrent acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening lower extremity pain, erythema, and swelling. He had recently missed doses of ruxolitinib, likely triggering a GVHD flare. Blood cultures revealed pseudomonas bacteremia, likely originating from chronically colonized leg wounds. He developed sepsis, acute hypoxic respiratory failure, and hospital-acquired pneumonia, requiring ICU admission, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and respiratory support with BiPAP and high-flow oxygen. His heart failure worsened with volume overload, necessitating aggressive diuresis. A new T4 compression fracture was identified, consistent with steroid-induced osteoporosis. Infectious disease guided antibiotic narrowing to ciprofloxacin, and his condition gradually improved over 24 days. He was discharged to extended care on IV ciprofloxacin, prednisone, ruxolitinib, and other baseline medications with plans for outpatient follow-up.

#Fever
#Chronic cellulitis, pseudomonas colonization
History of multiple hospitalizations for recurrent pseudomonas 
bacteremia. Presented with 1 week of fatigue and 1 day of chills 
with Tmax 100.0 at home. Most likely source felt to be his 
chronic cellulitis. He was started empirically on vancomycin and 
cefepime, while awaiting cultures. He was continued on home 
acyclovir, azithromycin, posaconazole, and atovaquone. His home 
amoxicillin and ciprofloxacin were held while on IV antibiotics. 
Cultures remained negative and he was afebrile x 48 hours, so he 
was transitioned to oral antibiotic therapy with ciprofloxacin 
500 mg BID, and doxycycline 100 mg BID. We continued to hold 
home amoxicillin. He was monitored for fevers which did recur. 
His blood cultures are still pending at time of discharge, but 
given his clinical stability, he is being discharged home to 
complete 7 day course of ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID and 
doxycycline 100 mg BID (end date ___.

#Shortness of breath
#HFrEF
History of HFrEF with LVEF ___ and evidence of moderate to 
severe global systolic dysfunction on latest ECHO (___). 
Dyspnea occurred in setting of receiving IVF and holding 
torsemide. The pt received Lasix 20 mg IV x 3 with improvement 
in his symptoms. Home toresemide was restarted and he continues 
to breath comfortably with good O2 saturation on room air.

#AML s/p Allo SCT/GVHD
Known GVHD of lungs and skin. Last PFTs in ___ with combined 
obstructive and restrictive defects. Diffuse GVHD of skin, 
currently on ruxolitinib and doing therapeutic maggot wound 
therapy through ___. Skin appears to be overall improving, 
although with continued evidence of chronic cellulitis. Wound 
cultures were performed on an open lesion on his right forearm, 
without evidence of active infection. He was evaluated by wound 
nurse. He was continued on home prednisone, sirolimus and 
ruxolitinib.

#Hypogammaglobulinemia
The patient usually receives ___ dose IVIG q2 weeks due to CHF. 
He did not receive this while inpatient. Should resume therapy 
at follow up appointment after discharge.

___
The etiology was felt most likely to be prerenal as kidney 
injury resolved with IVF. Cr improved from 1.6 to 1.2 on day of 
discharge.

#Hyperuricemia
Uric acid 12.3 without clear reason for tumor lysis. Most likely 
elevated in setting of ___. Improved with Rasburicase and IVF. 
Uric acid on day of discharge was 1.3.

#Hypothyroidism
He was continued home synthroid.

#Transaminitis
LFTs with mild elevation. Stable throughout admission and 
thought to be medication related. LFTs were monitored daily.

#Depression
He was continued home venlafaxine.

====================
- Pt was started on 7d course of ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID and 
doxycycline 100 mg BID (end date ___.
- Home amoxicillin was held while being treated, recommend 
restarting for prophylaxis after he finishes above antibiotics 
course. 
- Pt should also resume home dose of ciprofloxacin 250mg BID 
after he finishes the above antibiotics course.
- He should resume his IVIG treatments as an outpatient.
